carried.name: Programme Guide
carried.summary: Round 9: #1 by score (mean 8.11, in 8 judges' top fours); carried as the best score of the round (clearly different here means 6.0 or more apart; the round's median is 10.0). Family: programme listing. Born in round 9 (informed). The listing set on slate: every part is a band with its head column inside, every list is a one-line row read across a dotted leader to a column of facts, a denim needle marks where you are, and #6dff9c lights only where the machine is live. Magic Eye's programme-guide structure (head column, one-line timetable rows, the tuning scale and needle, the one-screen month, a seven-step type system in two widths), moved off the wine and the switched-off black margins onto Signal Galley's green-black slate. The head column now lives inside each slate band, so the margin is material rather than empty. The feel is a well-set TV listing or station timetable lit by one green tube: calm, grounded, readable in columns, and the bright phosphor is kept for the mark, Send, 'mind', focus, the live lamps and the monitors.

carried.name: Signal Legend
carried.summary:
Round 9: #2 by score (mean 7.51, in 7 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: ruled composing room; nearest carried Programme Guide at 7.59. Family: ruled composing room. Born in round 9 (informed). Signal Galley's green-black slate trays with every head set into its rail, reverse video for this one, square family surfaces against round machine glass, a thin case, and #6dff9c lit only for now and live. This is a refinement of Signal Galley. It keeps the slate trays, the one strip, the fortnight line with its breathing now lamp, the timetable margins and the masthead. On top of those it adds the grammar of an old text-mode program:
- Every tray's name, and its link, is knocked into its Oxford rail like a legend on a panel.
- 'This one' is always a quiet steel reverse-video block.
- What the family keeps is square; only the machine (the greeting glass, Vera's lines, the tubes and the cases) is rounded.

It should feel like a calm, well-labelled signal box at night. Grounded steel and slate carry the page, and the phosphor lights only what is live.

carried.name: Flight Deck
carried.summary: Round 9: #3 by score (mean 7.44, in 6 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: glass cockpit; nearest carried Signal Legend at 6.66. Family: glass cockpit. Born in round 9 (informed). A 1980s glass cockpit at night: the family's things on matte instrument plates grouped by fine demarcation lines with their legends set in the breaks, the machine on flush display units in thin screwed faceplates, and every colour holding one meaning from the EFIS code. The Phosphor Interface is drawn as the glass cockpit of about 1982. What the family owns sits on matte slate instrument plates. Each plate is grouped by one fine demarcation line: its legend is set in the line's break, its links sit at the right end, and the bracket turns down beside the rows and stays open on the right. What the machine shows sits on display units in thin, square, screwed faceplates. The page should feel quiet, exact and legible, like a flight deck at night: colour carries meaning instead of decoration, and #6dff9c lights only what is active or live.

carried.name: Reverse Video
carried.summary: Round 9: #5 by score (mean 7.09, in 4 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: text-mode windows; nearest carried Signal Legend at 6.34. Family: text-mode windows. Round 8: #2 by score (mean 7.86, in 7 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: text-mode windows; nearest carried Signal Galley at 6.69. Family: text-mode windows. Born in round 8 (informed). The page drawn in the grammar of the software that ran on green screens: flat steel windows with their names set into the frame, double-framed dialogs for what you act in, unboxed rows, a highlight bar that fades like a tube, and reverse video for where you are. The CRT is carried by the grammar of every frame, not by pictures or more green. Everything the family owns is a square steel window with its name knocked into an inset frame line, or a double-framed dialog when you act in it. Lists are unboxed rows that a steel highlight bar walks down and then fades from like phosphor, and 'this one' is always a reverse-video block. Rounded green-black glass stays for the machine alone: her greeting, her lines and the tubes. The bright #6dff9c appears only on the mark, Send and the primary buttons, the key word, focus rings, live lamps and the monitors, so the page feels like a calm old program running on a modern screen.

wildCarried.name: Attract Mode
wildCarried.summary: Round 9: #10 by score (mean 5.04, in 0 judges' top fours); carried as the wild lane, for the ideas the judges most want developed (3 promise votes, #10 by score, today 4.0): teal-tinted ground. Family: teal-tinted ground. Born in round 9 (random). An arcade after hours: graphite cabinets stacked in ruled bands across the page, keys with a little travel, fields sunk as wells, a teal night light, and the green only where a screen is running. The page is a dark arcade after closing. Graphite cabinets with a teal tint are stacked as full-width bands, each ruled from the next in its section's arcade-button colour. The only phosphor comes from the monitors, the mark, the Send key, the key word, focus and the live lights. It should feel quiet, solid and a little playful: raised things are keys you press, a key latched down means you are here, and sunk wells are where you type.

wildCarried.name: Porcelain Atlas
wildCarried.summary: Round 9: #11 by score (mean 5.0, in 0 judges' top fours); carried as the wild lane, for the ideas the judges most want developed (3 promise votes, #11 by score, today 4.0): porcelain star atlas. Family: porcelain star atlas. Born in round 9 (random). A star atlas set as a book: one centred column in Newsreader on a green-black dome, porcelain ink and cobalt hairlines, each part of the site a disc of its own star colour, the page you are on a star, and the phosphor kept for the console. The page is a planetarium's star atlas, bound as a book. It is one centred 45rem reading column with the night round it for margins: a cobalt zenith at the top, a few fixed stars in the margins only, and a green airglow rising off the horizon rule under Home's greeting. Porcelain ink, cobalt plates and hairlines, and low-chroma star colours do the everyday work. Marks now follow an atlas's magnitude scale: a disc for each part, a smaller disc for each kind, and an eight-rayed star for the page you are on. The exact #6dff9c is the operator's console: the mark and cursor, 'mind', Send and the primary buttons, focus, the live lights and the monitors. It should feel quiet, typeset and calm, with the green switched on only where the machine is.

brief.name: Mimic Panel
brief.hypothesis: The mimic-line grammar (one track per sequence, lamps as stops, a timetable margin, and #6dff9c only for now and live) was among the freshest structures in the hall of fame. Its record says it lost points on execution, not on the idea: plates floating on bare black, a one-sided chat, an action stranded on a line, rails that overran their last lamp, a lavender accent and a thin type scale. Built again with every one of those fixed and all of its lines kept, it should compete with the leaders on execution while keeping a structure none of them has.
brief.brief: START FROM the mimic-line design in the hall of fame: its palette /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r8/palettes/r7-idea-2.json and its templates /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r8/variants/r7-idea-2/ (read-only there; copy both to your id in this round). Its shots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r8/out/r7-idea-2/shots/, and every judge's scores, reasons and fixes for it are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r7/results.json and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r8/results.json under the id r7-idea-2: read them. KEEP ALL OF ITS LINES, as a system on every page: the bar's bottom rule with its dot under the current page; the page-head line that rings each page's icon and turns its rounded corner under the head; Home's horizontal Coming up track with the lit now lamp and ringed stops; the vertical To do track with its lamps and its timetable margin; Chat's thread hanging from Vera's mark and ending in a ring at the message box; the tracks on Status, Plans, setup and Sign in; and the lamp legend (hollow ring to come, lit sage for done, amber for needs a look, red for off, #6dff9c only for now and live). APPLY THE JUDGES' FIXES (informed mutations): (1) Ground the page: put the plates and the stops on a green-black slate tray behind each track section (about #0f1519 trays, #161c20 plates, edges #2e343b), Status's columns included, so grounded colour carries Home below the fold and Status rather than thin plates on bare black. Tint each idea plate faintly with its kind. (2) Chat keeps its track but gets its two sides back: the family's bubbles right of the track and flush right with a 3px accent bar, Vera's on green-black glass with a faint brand edge. (3) Ideas: keep the head line ringing the icon and holding the controls, but put 'Add an idea' on the title's baseline at the right, never on the line's elbow, and keep the tabs in source order after 'Save a thought'. (4) End every track on its last lamp: no rail runs past its final stop. (5) The timetable margin gets about 7.5rem and one-line stamps (nowrap). Below 40rem, fold the times into the plate head so the phone keeps its bubble measure. (6) Move the lavender and blue-pewter accent to a steel-cyan (about #a7c4d8, checked against every section floor), for links, rings and 'here'. (7) Keep the bar's dot, and also mark the current page clearly: its label in the heading colour and a short lit segment of the rule under it, centred on the dot. (8) Bring Lately added and the kids' wishes onto the track as stops (each kind's ring as the lamp), so the grammar holds on all of Home. (9) A real type scale: page titles clearly above section heads, section heads clearly above body; the rule under each masthead sits under the title, not the deck; one-line stamps in tabular mono. (10) Plates answer the pointer: a hover and the afterglow, as the other cards have. Nowrap Next up's '4 more on the radar' line and the radar's distances. To do's edit folds at 2.75rem targets. (11) A thinner, squarer monitor case with fine detail (a groove, vents, a power LED) rather than the thick rounded pewter slab. NAME: give it a new name of two or three words. Its tagline, concept, companions, strengths and weaknesses describe the design on its own terms, without naming any earlier entrant or its id.
brief.borrows: The mimic-line design (r7-idea-2) in full, with its lines; Signal Galley's slate trays; the judges' recorded fixes from rounds 7 and 8.
brief.avoids: Plates on bare black, the one-sided chat, 'Add an idea' on the elbow, rails overrunning their last lamp, the lavender accent, the thin type scale, the thick case.
